execution_rule: Execute exactly one ready task at a time in listed order. Only tasks whose scope is allowed by EXECUTION-SCOPE.yaml may execute.

tasks.title: Verify specification pack and execution scope
steps: Run sha256sum -c docs/plan/SUPPORTING-DOCS.sha256.
Run python3 scripts/verify-plan-contract.py.
Read CLAUDE.md, this plan, EXECUTION-SCOPE.yaml, SOURCE-REFERENCE-INDEX.yaml, and the complete task manifest before modifying source code.
Confirm execution_scope.release equals pilot-v3-foundation and allowed_scope contains NOW only.
If either preflight command fails, a required document is missing, a source reference cannot be resolved, or scope differs, create docs/blockers/P0.1.md using the blocker template and stop.

Do not create source crates before preflight passes.

tasks.title: Create Rust and UI workspace skeleton
steps: Create the workspace members exactly as listed in the target repository layout in this plan.
Write rust-toolchain.toml exactly as: [toolchain] channel="1.98.1", profile="minimal", components=["rustfmt","clippy","llvm-tools-preview"].
Write .node-version containing exactly `24.21.0` followed by one newline.
Set ui/package.json `engines` exactly to {"node":"24.21.0","npm":"11.19.0"} and `packageManager` exactly to "npm@11.19.0".
Set ui/package.json scripts at P0.2 exactly to {"typecheck":"tsc --noEmit"}. U0.1 later replaces/extends the scripts block with its fully specified UI scripts.

Set ui/package.json install-script policy exactly to "allowScripts": {"msw": false}. MSW's postinstall worker synchronization is not required by the P0.2 skeleton and must not execute. Any other package with an unreviewed install script must make P0.2 block.
Copy the exact [workspace.dependencies] and crate dependency matrix from this plan into Cargo.toml files; crate Cargo.toml files must use workspace = true and may not alter versions/features.

Install exactly the versioned UI runtime and development packages listed in §§5.2-5.3 with npm using --save-exact --strict-peer-deps --strict-allow-scripts, apply the JavaScript dependency installation policy in §5.3.1, and commit ui/package-lock.json. Do not add any other package. Do not use --ignore-scripts, --force, --legacy-peer-deps, --dangerously-allow-all-scripts or npm overrides, and do not regenerate the lockfile with npm install --package-lock-only.

Create Makefile targets with these exact P0.2 behaviors:

- check: run cargo check --workspace, then ui-check
- test: run cargo test --workspace
- ui-check: run cd ui && npm run typecheck
- cov: run cargo llvm-cov --workspace --summary-only
- mutants: run cargo mutants --workspace
- openapi: run test -f api/modeller.openapi.json
- e2e: run test -f tests/e2e_hr.rs
- all: depend on check and test

The openapi and e2e targets are deliberate readiness checks. They are expected to return failure until the later tasks responsible for those artifacts create them. Do not put unfinished implementation markers or dummy commands into these targets.
Create CI on ubuntu-24.04 using actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-node@v4 with node-version 24.21.0; install npm@11.19.0; install Rust 1.98.1 with rustfmt, clippy, llvm-tools-preview.
CI verifies the native C toolchain by running cc --version; the ubuntu-24.04 runner remains the pinned CI operating-system baseline.
CI installs cargo-llvm-cov exactly 0.9.1 and cargo-mutants exactly 27.1.0 using cargo install --version ... --locked.
If local node --version is not v24.21.0 or npm --version is not 11.19.0, stop with BLOCKED-ENVIRONMENT rather than using a different version.
acceptance: rustc --version starts with `rustc 1.98.1`; node --version equals `v24.21.0`; npm --version equals `11.19.0`.
Workspace compiles with empty crates; Cargo.lock and ui/package-lock.json are committed; CI workflow uses the exact pinned toolchain and runner.

tasks.title: Implement core IDs, clock, canonical JSON and hashes
steps: Implement Id as a validated String newtype exactly per plan §6.3: grammar ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(?::[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)*$, no trimming or normalization, exact string preserved, validated FromStr and TryFrom<String>, Display, AsRef<str>, as_str(), and serde deserialization that rejects invalid strings.

Implement Hash as one validated String newtype exactly per plan §6.3 accepting only sha256:<64 lowercase hex>, psg:sha256:<64 lowercase hex> and ev:sha256:<64 lowercase hex>; provide HashKind {Generic, Semantic, Evidence}, Hash::kind(), Hash::content_sha256(&[u8]), Hash::semantic_sha256(&[u8]), Hash::evidence_sha256(&[u8]), validated FromStr and TryFrom<String>, Display, AsRef<str>, as_str(), and validating serde deserialization. Do not create separate SemanticHash or EvidenceHash types.

Implement Timestamp(time::OffsetDateTime) exactly per plan §6.3 (UTC-normalized; RFC 3339 input with T or single-space separator and offset conversion; surrounding whitespace rejected; UTC year restricted to 0000..=9999 with rejection, never panic, outside it; nanosecond precision; canonical Display/serialization with uppercase T, uppercase Z and exactly nine fractional digits) and the Clock trait with fn now(&self) -> Timestamp, SystemClock and FixedClock.

Implement the canonical JSON primitive by applying RFC 8785 JCS through the explicitly allowed serde_json_canonicalizer dependency (serde_json_canonicalizer::to_vec) to the supplied value. Do not implement Plumb domain-specific ordering of semantically unordered arrays in F0.1; later semantic-envelope construction applies it before calling this primitive.
Implement sha256 hashing over canonical bytes.
Do not include timestamps, layout metadata, or audit metadata in semantic hash input; the exact semantic envelope is defined by the metamodel.
Add deterministic property tests that map insertion order does not affect canonical output or hash.

Tests cover at minimum:

- Id: every plan §6.3 valid and invalid example; serialization round-trip; invalid serde deserialization rejection.
- Hash: all three accepted prefixes; exactly 64 lowercase hex; uppercase rejection; length rejection; unknown-prefix rejection; HashKind; deterministic SHA-256 constructors.
- Timestamp: UTC serialization; non-UTC offset normalization; exactly nine fractional digits; nanosecond retention; serde round-trip; FixedClock repeatability; space-separator input serializing back with T; surrounding-whitespace rejection; valid boundary years 0000 and 9999; rejection below and above the representable range where constructible (including offset normalization past either bound); offset normalization that stays inside the range.
- Canonical JSON/hash: every plan §6.3 RFC 8785 conformance fixture produces its fixed expected bytes (ASCII, quote/backslash, control-character, BMP and non-BMP keys, string escaping, numbers); each expected output is a fixed point; map insertion order produces byte-identical output and equal resulting hashes, including property tests; repeated canonicalization is byte-identical.
acceptance: Canonical output is byte-identical for semantically identical map insertion orders and all tests pass.
Id, Hash and Timestamp satisfy every plan §6.3 grammar, example and canonicalization rule, and serde deserialization of invalid Id/Hash/Timestamp values fails.
Every plan §6.3 RFC 8785 conformance fixture produces exactly its fixed expected bytes, and each expected output canonicalizes to itself.
forbidden: Do not write a custom approximate JCS serializer.
Do not use wall-clock time directly outside SystemClock.
tasks.commit_message: F0.1: Implement core IDs, clock, canonical JSON and hashes

tasks.title: Implement content-addressed artifact model and SQLite artifact store
steps: Implement ArtifactKind exactly for source-original, source-extracted, evidence-manifest, inference-request, inference-response, validated-inference, external-validation, projection, proposal, patch, diff, impact-report, gate-report, conformance-report, scenario-trace, test-receipt, architecture-check.
Artifact identity is sha256 of stored bytes; duplicate put returns the existing hash.
Create SQLite table artifacts(hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY, kind TEXT NOT NULL, media_type TEXT NOT NULL, bytes BLOB NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL).
Artifact bytes are immutable; no update method is permitted.
Provide put/get/exists and transaction-safe duplicate insertion.
acceptance: Putting identical bytes twice returns the same hash and stores one row; differing bytes return differing hashes.
forbidden: Do not store mutable semantic state in the artifact table.
tasks.commit_message: F0.2: Implement content-addressed artifact model and SQLite artifact store

tasks.title: Implement PSG base envelope and typed status/standards structures
steps: Implement ElementStatus exactly: Proposed, Accepted, Rejected, Superseded, Deprecated, Suspect.
Implement StandardMapping, MappingRole and MappingStrength exactly from the metamodel.
Implement Node and Edge envelopes with immutable id, revision, status, evidence refs, derivation refs, standards, tags, extensions and audit metadata.
Extensions require a namespace-qualified key containing one colon.
Do not add a universal confidence field to Node or Edge.
acceptance: All base structures round-trip through JSON and reject an extension key without a namespace.
forbidden: Do not implement core semantics as kind:String plus arbitrary props.
Do not add fields absent from the metamodel without a blocking spec issue.
tasks.commit_message: F0.3: Implement PSG base envelope and typed status/standards structures

tasks.title: Implement complete NodePayload semantic enum
steps: Implement every core NodePayload variant defined by the metamodel namespaces: evidence/provenance, governance, intent/requirements, vocabulary/domain, functional behavior, authorization, quality, architecture, technical contracts, delivery, verification, standards profile and view model.
Field names, required/optional status, and enums must follow the metamodel sections defining each type.
Use serde tagged representation type/data as specified by metamodel §24.
When the prose definition and skeleton disagree, do not choose; create docs/blockers/F0.4.md identifying both conflicting passages and stop.

tasks.commit_message: F0.4: Implement complete NodePayload semantic enum

tasks.title: Implement RelationKind and typed relation registry
steps: Implement the closed core relation vocabulary exactly from metamodel §17.
For each relation register allowed source NodePayload types, allowed target types, cardinality constraints and graph constraints.
Support namespaced extension relations separately; core code must reject an unknown unqualified relation.
Validate acyclicity for supersedes, refines/decomposes_to where mandated, inherits_role, and depends_on_slice.
acceptance: Every relation listed in metamodel §17 has a registry entry; invalid source/target pairs are rejected; required acyclic relations reject cycles.
forbidden: Do not infer relation compatibility from type names.
tasks.commit_message: F0.5: Implement RelationKind and typed relation registry

tasks.title: Implement Graph, typed indexes and semantic/evidence hashes
steps: Implement BTreeMap-backed node and edge storage.
Maintain indexes by payload type, relation kind, outgoing node and incoming node.
Graph validation calls node schema validation, relation registry validation and mandatory core invariants applicable without gate context.
Implement semantic_hash over accepted semantic nodes/edges plus accepted semantic decisions/constraints using exclusions defined by metamodel §3.1.
Implement evidence_hash over source artifacts/evidence identity.
View/layout data must not influence semantic_hash.
acceptance: Graph hash is stable across insertion order; changing audit timestamp or view position does not change semantic_hash; changing an accepted requirement statement does.
forbidden: Do not hash transient compile jobs or cached inference text into semantic_hash.
tasks.commit_message: F0.6: Implement Graph, typed indexes and semantic/evidence hashes

tasks.title: Implement serializable SemanticPatch AST and deterministic apply/diff
steps: Implement AddNode, RemoveNode, ReplacePayload, SetStatus, AddEdge, RemoveEdge, MergeNodes, Supersede, AttachEvidence, AttachStandardMapping and Compound exactly as metamodel §20.
Every destructive operation carries the expected current semantic hash or expected element hash required by the metamodel.
Apply patches to an immutable Graph input and return GraphDelta plus new Graph.
Provide deterministic structured diff sorted by element ID and operation order.
Implement inverse only for patch operations where an exact inverse is derivable from the patch input; do not fabricate an inverse.
acceptance: All patch variants serialize/deserialize; apply is deterministic; property tests cover applicable apply/invert round trips.
forbidden: Do not use Box<dyn Patch>.
Do not mutate Graph in place.
tasks.commit_message: F0.7: Implement serializable SemanticPatch AST and deterministic apply/diff

tasks.title: Implement immutable revision store, branch heads and CAS commit
steps: Create SQLite tables graph_revisions, revision_nodes, revision_edges, branch_heads and ledger_events using the exact schema block in this plan.
A GraphRevision is immutable and stores global numeric version, parent revision, semantic_hash, evidence_hash, profile_ref, rule_pack_hash, patch artifact ref, decision refs, creator and timestamp.
Assign version 1 to the initial revision and max(version)+1 to each successful new revision inside the same SQLite transaction.
Set revision ID to `rev:<version>:<first16-semantic-hash-hex>`.
Implement create_initial_revision, load_revision, head, create_branch, commit(branch, expected_head, patch), and move_head for explicit restore.
commit must be one SQLite transaction and fail with STALE_BASE when expected_head differs.
Persist full graph snapshot per revision for the pilot; do not introduce delta storage.
acceptance: Concurrent commits against the same expected head allow exactly one success; restore is implemented by branch-head movement and does not delete history.
forbidden: Do not overwrite an existing revision.
Do not silently rebase a stale patch.
tasks.commit_message: F0.8: Implement immutable revision store, branch heads and CAS commit

tasks.title: Implement provenance DerivationRecord and inference artifact contracts
steps: Implement Agent, DerivationRecord, InferenceRequest and InferenceArtifact fields exactly from metamodel §5 and compiler architecture §4.3-4.4.
InferenceRequest ID is deterministic from canonical request content.
NullProvider always returns a typed provider-disabled error.
MockProvider returns only artifacts supplied explicitly by a test fixture keyed by request hash.
A live provider interface returns an InferenceArtifact and has no access to GraphStore or branch commits.
acceptance: Request hashes are deterministic; replaying a MockProvider fixture produces the same validated_output_hash.
forbidden: Do not permit provider code to mutate PSG.
Do not call a live network provider in tests.
tasks.commit_message: F0.9: Implement provenance DerivationRecord and inference artifact contracts

tasks.title: Implement compiler stage plan/evaluate contract and compile-run records
steps: Implement CompilerStage::plan and CompilerStage::evaluate exactly as compiler architecture §28.
Implement StagePlan, StageEvaluation and CompileRun.
plan and evaluate receive no network/client dependency and must be deterministic for equal inputs/artifacts.
Artifact acquisition is represented by requests returned in StagePlan and executed by orchestration code outside the trait.
Persist compile-run metadata as an artifact; do not make operational timestamps part of semantic output hash.
acceptance: A fixture stage returns identical plan/evaluation bytes for repeated equal inputs and cannot access an InferenceProvider through the stage trait.
forbidden: Do not add complete_json or HTTP calls to CompilerStage.
tasks.commit_message: F0.10: Implement compiler stage plan/evaluate contract and compile-run records

tasks.title: Implement impact seed and dirty-set reachability
steps: For each GraphDelta compute ChangedSet containing touched node and edge IDs.

Compute DirtySet through typed graph relations that participate in semantic dependency: derived_from, specified_by, constrained_by, satisfied_by, reads, writes, governed_by, uses_calculation, allocated_to, exposed_by, implemented_by, verified_by and implemented_as.
Return affected projections and affected gate namespaces as symbolic sets; full C1 evidence staleness remains post-pilot.
Traversal order must be deterministic.
acceptance: Changing a calculation marks dependent operations and scenarios dirty; changing only view metadata marks no semantic element dirty.
forbidden: Do not use name similarity for impact propagation.
tasks.commit_message: F0.11: Implement impact seed and dirty-set reachability

tasks.title: Implement standards profile loader and validation rule metadata
steps: Load profile metadata from the supplied YAML without modifying that YAML.
Implement RuleClass, RuleResultState, Severity, WaiverPolicy, GateId and StandardRef.
At startup validate that the YAML contains exactly the 133 rule IDs from the supplied file and unique IDs.
For NOW scope register evaluator functions only for gates I0, F1, F2, F3 and F4; metadata for later gates must still load.
A missing evaluator for a NOW rule is startup error; a missing evaluator for a later gate returns NOT_IMPLEMENTED if that gate is explicitly requested.
acceptance: All 133 metadata rules load; exactly 54 NOW gate rules require evaluators; duplicate rule IDs fail profile loading.
forbidden: Do not rewrite rule IDs or severities in code.
Do not duplicate rule metadata in Rust constants when it can be loaded from YAML.
tasks.commit_message: F0.12: Implement standards profile loader and validation rule metadata

tasks.title: Implement deterministic gate evaluator, findings and waivers
steps: Implement rule result states PASS, FAIL, WARN, NOT_APPLICABLE, WAIVED, ERROR.
Finding key is sha256(rule_id || sorted(target_ids) || semantic_condition_key).
Gate passes only under rulebook §2 semantics.
WAIVED requires rule waiver policy plus an accepted ResolutionDecision reference; forbidden waivers fail.
GateReport includes baseline semantic_hash, profile ID/hash, rule-pack hash, individual rule results and waiver list.
Evaluation is pure; external validation artifacts are inputs, never executed inside evaluator.
acceptance: Repeated gate evaluation over equal graph/profile/artifacts is byte-identical except explicitly excluded operational timestamp fields.
forbidden: Do not let readiness scores influence gate result.
tasks.commit_message: F0.13: Implement deterministic gate evaluator, findings and waivers

tasks.title: Implement functional.yaml v2 compatibility projection from PSG
steps: Implement the v2 functional.yaml shape exactly as v2 plan §4.1 as an output projection only.

Map PSG Actor/BusinessRole/SecurityRole/Permission to the legacy actor/role representation without losing PSG truth; any lossy mapping must be documented in projection metadata and never written back automatically.
Map QualityScenario to legacy NFR fields only where an exact legacy field exists; omit unsupported quality scenarios from the legacy NFR bag and list them in projection warnings.
Validate the projection against schemas/functional-v2.schema.json.
Projection metadata records source semantic_hash, profile_hash, projection version and content hash.
acceptance: Golden HR projection is deterministic and validates; modifying UI layout does not change projection content.
forbidden: Do not treat functional.yaml as canonical input state.
tasks.commit_message: F0.14: Implement functional.yaml v2 compatibility projection from PSG

tasks.title: Implement Markdown and plain-text source import
steps: Import bytes into SourceArtifact with source_kind, display_name, content_hash and media_type.
Decode UTF-8; reject invalid UTF-8 for .md/.txt with E_SOURCE_ENCODING. Normalize CRLF and CR to LF; do not trim internal whitespace.
Create a content-addressed source-extracted artifact from the normalized UTF-8 text.
Markdown heading fragment: one ATX heading matching `^#{1,6}[ \t]+(.+?)\s*$`; fragment includes the full normalized source line.
Markdown unordered-list fragment: one line matching `^[ \t]*[-+*][ \t]+(.+)$`; ordered-list fragment: one line matching `^[ \t]*[0-9]+[.)][ \t]+(.+)$`.

Markdown table fragment: a contiguous pipe-delimited block is a table only when its second nonblank line matches a GFM delimiter row whose cells match `^:?-{3,}:?$`; emit one EvidenceFragment per subsequent data row and include header cells in fragment metadata.
Paragraph fragment: maximal contiguous nonblank lines not already classified as heading/list/table; preserve embedded newlines.
Plain-text import emits paragraph fragments using the same paragraph rule and ordered/unordered list recognition; it has no heading or table inference.
TextRange start/end are zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets into normalized extracted text with end exclusive; slicing those bytes must equal the exact fragment text.
acceptance: All classification regexes above are covered by tests; fragment ranges round-trip exactly; no other Markdown construct receives a special fragment kind in NOW scope.
tasks.commit_message: S0.1: Implement Markdown and plain-text source import

tasks.title: Implement deterministic minimal DOCX importer
steps: Implement DOCX parsing over zip/XML for paragraphs, headings, numbered lists, bulleted lists and tables with row/header extraction.
Use only zip and quick-xml from the allowed dependency set.
Preserve extracted-text order; merged cells must resolve deterministically.
Unsupported DOCX content becomes a parse warning with source locator; it must not be silently dropped when it contains visible text.
Use the bundled read-only fixtures/hr-leave/requirements.docx as one acceptance input; do not edit it.
acceptance: The HR DOCX extracts the expected ordered text and tables; unsupported visible text creates a warning.
tasks.commit_message: S0.2: Implement deterministic minimal DOCX importer

tasks.title: Implement evidence manifest and I0 evaluator functions
steps: Implement all six I0 rules from the supplied rule YAML and rulebook without changing IDs, severity or waiver policy.
Evidence manifest lists source artifact refs, extracted artifact refs, fragment refs and hashes in sorted order.
PPMN.I0.PROVENANCE.AGENT_IDENTIFIED passes only when every derivation-producing action identifies an Agent.
PLUMB.I0.BASELINE.HASHABLE validates reproducible evidence_hash.
acceptance: All six I0 rule fixtures cover PASS and FAIL; HR source corpus passes I0.
tasks.commit_message: S0.3: Implement evidence manifest and I0 evaluator functions

tasks.title: Implement segmentation request/artifact pipeline and deterministic fallback
steps: Create an InferenceRequest for semantic segmentation anchored only to EvidenceFragment IDs and extracted text.
Validate inference output against the JSON schema before evaluate uses it.
Implement deterministic fallback: one candidate per list item or sentence containing shall, must, should or can.
Post-check fragment coverage, overlap and locator validity; unassigned text is explicitly classified non-requirement and flagged.
A failed or absent inference artifact uses fallback; this operational fallback must be recorded in DerivationRecord.
acceptance: Mock artifact path and fallback path produce valid, non-overlapping candidates; a gap produces the declared intake uncovered error.
forbidden: Do not call an LLM from segment evaluation.
Do not create a requirement without an EvidenceFragment reference.
tasks.commit_message: S0.4: Implement segmentation request/artifact pipeline and deterministic fallback

tasks.title: Implement Requirement, Need, Goal, Concern and Constraint compilation
steps: Compile candidate requirement statements into Proposed Requirement nodes with evidence.
Use deterministic modality extraction for shall, should, may and shall not; any other normative interpretation is a proposal requiring human confirmation.
Classification inference may propose requirement_kind and level but evaluate rejects values outside metamodel enums.
Create optional Need/Goal/Concern/Constraint proposals only when they contain evidence refs.
Requirement IDs are deterministic from project namespace plus stable evidence fragment key; re-import of unchanged evidence preserves IDs.
acceptance: Re-import preserves IDs; classification outside enum is rejected; no accepted requirement lacks evidence or explicit human-origin derivation.
tasks.commit_message: S1.1: Implement Requirement, Need, Goal, Concern and Constraint compilation

tasks.title: Implement EARS normalization as non-authoritative proposal
steps: Store original requirement statement unchanged.
EARS-form normalized text is a Proposal that references the original requirement and evidence.
Accepting an EARS proposal uses SemanticPatch ReplacePayload and records ResolutionDecision when meaning changes materially.
Reject an EARS output that introduces an actor, trigger, condition, response or numeric constraint not grounded in evidence or already accepted PSG semantics.
acceptance: A crafted inference that invents a numeric threshold is rejected; original text remains retrievable after accepted normalization.
tasks.commit_message: S1.2: Implement EARS normalization as non-authoritative proposal

tasks.title: Implement duplicate detection and supersession proposals
steps: Implement normalized Jaccard duplicate score using the threshold from profile configuration.
Return duplicate/near-duplicate findings and merge/supersede proposals; never auto-merge accepted requirements.
Use MergeNodes only when the two requirements assert the same active obligation and neither is identified as a later replacement; preserve evidence from both.
Use Supersede only when evidence or an explicit human decision identifies one requirement as replacing the other; preserve both nodes and the supersedes relation.
acceptance: Exact duplicate fixture is detected deterministically; accepting merge preserves all evidence references.
tasks.commit_message: S1.3: Implement duplicate detection and supersession proposals

tasks.title: Implement deterministic requirement lint pack and corpus benchmark
steps: Implement the 15 pilot lint rules listed in v2 M2.1 with stable IDs.
Each lint result references exact EvidenceFragment range.
Benchmark precision/recall per rule; if measured precision is below 0.85, effective severity is warn through configuration, not code mutation.
Regression test fails if precision drops by more than 0.03 from baseline.
acceptance: All 15 rule fixtures pass and the 200-sentence corpus baseline is committed with annotator agreement metadata.
tasks.commit_message: S1.4: Implement deterministic requirement lint pack and corpus benchmark

tasks.title: Implement vocabulary normalization and typed concept proposals
steps: Implement NFKC, case normalization, determiner stripping and the explicit singularization exception table stored in crates/plumb-functional/src/vocabulary_exceptions.rs.
Generate Term candidates with frequency and co-occurrence.
Inference may propose Concept kind only from object_type, fact_type, value_type, role, other.
Conflicting type proposals create findings; they do not overwrite accepted concepts.
acceptance: Vocabulary output is deterministic and HR reference typing reaches the v2 target where fixture labels exist.
tasks.commit_message: S1.5: Implement vocabulary normalization and typed concept proposals

tasks.title: Implement all F1 validation rules
steps: Implement all eleven F1 evaluators from the supplied rule YAML and rulebook.
Each evaluator returns target IDs and deterministic semantic_condition_key.
Rules classified external_standard use the supplied metadata only; code must not claim clause-level compliance.
F1 gate result must include unresolved lint blockers, vocabulary blockers, duplicates and contradictions.
acceptance: All eleven F1 rules have PASS and FAIL fixtures; HR requirements baseline reaches F1 only after required fixture resolutions.
tasks.commit_message: S1.6: Implement all F1 validation rules

tasks.title: Implement entity, attribute and domain-relationship proposals
steps: Inference proposals are closed to accepted vocabulary Concept IDs; unknown terms are rejected and returned as findings.
Attributes require owning Entity, value_type and nullable.
DomainRelationship cardinality is populated only when stated or later human-resolved; inference cannot silently choose missing cardinality.
Consolidation produces MergeNodes proposals, never direct mutation.
acceptance: Unknown vocabulary is rejected; accepted attribute has exactly one owner; HR entity survival meets the v2 fixture target.
tasks.commit_message: S2.1: Implement entity, attribute and domain-relationship proposals

tasks.title: Implement states, transitions and invariants
steps: Create State and Transition proposals from lifecycle evidence.
Transition requires stateful_ref, from_state, to_state and trigger_ref; missing trigger is a finding/question.
Invariant expressions are PlumbExpr proposals and cannot become Accepted until parse/typecheck succeeds.
No lifecycle state is inferred solely from capitalization or field names.
acceptance: State graph rejects missing endpoints/trigger; HR state fixture validates.
tasks.commit_message: S2.2: Implement states, transitions and invariants

tasks.title: Implement data classification dictionary proposals
steps: Implement explicit deterministic dictionary entries for the v2 pilot examples including email, dob, salary and iban.
Dictionary hit creates proposed classification with deterministic derivation.
Unknown classification may be proposed by inference only through a separate proposal; absence remains unknown rather than defaulting to none.
acceptance: Known dictionary values classify deterministically; unknown values remain unresolved until accepted proposal/decision.
tasks.commit_message: S2.3: Implement data classification dictionary proposals

tasks.title: Implement PlumbExpr grammar and typed AST
steps: Implement literals, dotted identifiers, arithmetic, comparisons, boolean operators, calls, in and lists exactly as v2 M5.1.
Implement Ty variants exactly as inherited v2 type contract unless contradicted by metamodel; preserve Decimal precision, Date, DateTime, Duration, Quantity, Enum, Ref and List.
Parser never executes code and exposes no scripting escape.

If no HR object qualifies, generate the example recursively from the OpenAPI schema with this exact rule: enum -> lexicographically first serialized enum value; boolean -> true; integer -> schema minimum else 1; number -> schema minimum else 1.0; string/date -> `2026-01-15`; string/date-time -> `2026-01-15T12:00:00Z`; other string -> `example`; array -> one generated item; object -> all required properties only, in lexicographic property-name order; oneOf/anyOf -> branch with lexicographically smallest RFC-8785 canonical schema JSON; nullable is ignored when a non-null branch exists.

Generated examples must validate against the generated schema. If a format/pattern/constraint makes the deterministic fallback invalid and no HR example exists, stop A0.1 with BLOCKED-TEST-CONTRACT naming the endpoint/schema; do not invent a value.
GET /api/model/version response is {version, hash, revision, semantic_hash, evidence_hash}; version/hash are compatibility aliases of revision/semantic_hash.
GET /api/gates returns I0, F1, F2, F3, F4 in this order; later gates are omitted in NOW scope.
Every write request requires If-Match containing current semantic_hash; 412 response includes current revision and semantic_hash.
Job responses include base_revision and stale status.
